transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Falcon CTO), Ethan Rivera (Falcon SRE), Priya Kapoor (Falcon Security)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 6-week pilot to validate security gates (SOC2/ISO), SSO/SAM EL integration, RBAC, audit logs, and run throughput/latency benchmarks against Falcon Retail's checkout and recommendation flows. Primary concerns: data residency, secrets/K M S, and deterministic rollbacks if quality regressions.

Topics covered:
- Pilot success criteria and acceptance tests
- Workload sizing and sample payloads
- Benchmarks: p99 latency, tokens/sec, concurrency, batch sizing, quantization tradeoffs
- Security/compliance: SOC 2, ISO27001, SSO/SAM el, RBAC, audit logs, K M S / H S M options
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena: okay, good morning everyone thanks for taking the time, uh this is lena from Redwood. we put together a short agenda, run through security gates, bench targets, and a proposed timeline for the pilot.
[00:18] Maya: thanks lena, excited to dig in. quick context, we are a mid-size retail platform, very sensitive to PII in order data and logs, plus we have european customers so data residency matters.
[00:31] Ethan: yes, and from infra side we need to know if the pilot can run in our V P C and how logs are exported, retention, that sort of thing.
[00:40] Diego: totally, we'll cover private deployment options and what we can expose for audit logs. quick note: when we say hosted vs dedicated, hosted is fast, but dedicated/reserved gives you more isolation and predictable throughput.
[00:55] Priya: on compliance side we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and an ISO 27001 cert, plus a clear SSO / Sam el integration story. RBAC mapping from our AD is a must.
[01:10] Lena: yep, we can share SOC 2 and the ISO artefacts, plus our SOC 2 audit contact. we'll also include our pen test summary.
[01:19] Maya: what about K M S? we need customer-managed keys or H S M option for production.
[01:26] Diego: for the pilot we can demo K M S integration with customer keys in a VPC private deployment. for hosted we support envelope encryption and can integrate with external K M S for dedicated or private.
[01:40] Ethan: how about logs? we need immutable audit trails, ideally shipped to our SIEM via syslog/s3.
[01:47] Diego: yes, we can forward audit logs to s3 or a SIEM; we have an audit log mode that includes request/response headers and non-sensitive metadata. note we redact model outputs by default, but binary artifacts may require special handling.
[02:05] Priya: we also need RBAC scopes mapped to our groups, can you support SCIM provisioning?
[02:12] Lena: we do support S C I M for user provisioning, SSO via SAML or OIDC, and role based access controls that can be mapped to AD groups. there may be small mapping work but it's standard.
[02:25] Maya: ok good. switching gears to benchmarks — our main flows are a short prompt checkout call (avg 64 tokens) and a recommendation generator (avg 420 tokens). peak qps around 350 for checkout during sales windows.
[02:40] Diego: helpful. for bench we want to run both: 1) short prompt latency (p50/p95/p99) at your target concurrency, 2) longer sequence throughput and effective tokens/sec. we'll propose a config with batching and an initial quantization profile.
[03:00] Ethan: what p99 should we expect for short prompts? our target is < 200ms ideally, but we know that depends on model choice and routing.
[03:10] Diego: accepted. for a trimmed model and dedicated GPUs we often see p99 in the 150-300ms range for 32-64 token responses; with larger sequences p99 will grow. we can aim for a pilot target of p99 < 300ms for checkout and median < 100ms for the simplest path.
[03:30] Priya: if the p99 misses, will we get automatic fallbacks to smaller models? we need deterministic behavior.
[03:36] Lena: yes, we support routing policies — can fall back to a lower-cost model or cached response. we'll include fallback rules in the runbook so your SREs can understand behavior.
[03:49] Maya: acceptance criteria, suggest we tie success to 1) security artifacts in place, 2) p99 latency target met for checkout at target concurrency, 3) no data leakage in logs, and 4) a quality gate for recommendation accuracy not declining more than 5% vs baseline.
[04:05] Lena: that sounds reasonable. we'll capture those as the acceptance tests.
[04:10] Ethan: timeline? we'd like to run the pilot in early January, with a 2-week benchmark window and a 4-week integration/validate window.
[04:20] Diego: proposed schedule: week 0 - kickoff & account setup, week 1 - security review and baseline benchmarks, week 2 - load tests and regression evals, weeks 3-4 - integration, RBAC and S S O testing, final acceptance at week 6.
[04:38] Maya: can Redwood run the load tests in our V P C or do we need to export traffic?
[04:44] Diego: we can run in your VPC with an ephemeral connector, or run from Redwood dedicated infra hitting a staging endpoint. the VPC path gives more fidelity for the pilot.
[04:55] Priya: on the K M S note, do you require key material or just integration? we prefer not to hand over key material.
[05:02] Lena: we don't require keys; we integrate via your KMS endpoints and use envelope encryption so the key material stays in your H S M or cloud K M S.
[05:12] Ethan: for benchmarks, can you capture token-level cost/latency breakdowns and provide per-route dashboards?
[05:18] Diego: yes, Redwood Console will give token cost, latency heatmaps, and per-route traces. we'll include a benchmark spreadsheet with cost modeling.
[05:28] Maya: any blockers on compliance? timelines for SOC2 artifacts?
[05:33] Lena: SOC 2 Type II report is available — we'll attach it. ISO 27001 cert is current, we'll attach that too, plus our data processing addendum and standard contract language.
[05:45] Priya: we need evidence of pen test recency and the contact for the auditor.
[05:50] Lena: will include pen test summary and auditor contact.
[05:54] Ethan: curious about secrets in logs — you mentioned redaction, but we need an explicit guarantee that full payment card PANs are never logged.
[06:03] Diego: we redact PII and have configurable redaction patterns; for PCI we recommend tokenizing/stripping at the application boundary and not sending raw PANs to the model. we'll include guidance in the runbook.
[06:18] Maya: on rollout, after pilot, we want an A/B compare window and a rollback plan if model quality drops.
[06:25] Lena: rollout tools support canarying, A/B tests, and automatic fallback with alerts. we'll show an example policy in the runbook.
[06:35] Priya: are audit logs immutable? we need tamper-evidence for some records.
[06:40] Diego: we can ship logs to your S3 with write-once policy or to SIEM that enforces immutability. we also support signed log export for tamper-evidence.
[06:52] Maya: good. one more: data residency — we need eu-only processing for EU customer data.
[06:58] Lena: we can pin requests to EU regions for hosted scenarios or run private deployment in your EU region. we'll document region pinning in the pilot config.
[07:08] Ethan: what about SSO and provisioning — timeline to enable SAML and SCIM?
[07:13] Diego: SAML setup is usually a 2-3 day config; SCIM provisioning adds another week if you want automated provisioning. for pilot we can do manual invites and later enable SCIM.
[07:26] Priya: ok that works.

[07:30] BENCHMARK DETAILS DISCUSSED
[07:31] Diego: I'll propose an initial benchmark config: model X-small / X-medium split, quantized FP16 or int8 profile, batch sizes 4/8 for checkout, 1-2 GPUs per worker, target 64 concurrent for short prompt bench and 16 concurrency for recommendation flow, sequence lengths 64 and 420 respectively. we'll also include KV cash (sic) warmup scenarios.
[07:54] Maya: note that our recommendation generator hits a heavy attention pattern; please watch memory and cache eviction.
[08:02] Diego: noted, we'll include KV cache warmup and eviction patterns in the runbook.

[08:15] TIMELINE & ACCEPTANCE
[08:16] Lena: recap of acceptance criteria: SOC2/ISO artifacts received, SSO/Saml flow validated, RBAC mapping tested, audit logs delivered to SIEM, p99 latency target for checkout met at target concurrency, recommendation accuracy within 5% of baseline, and clear K M S integration for secrets.
[08:40] Maya: agreed.

[08:44] CLOSING / NEXT STEPS
[08:45] Lena: action items recap: I'll send security packet (SOC2, ISO, pen test summary), Diego will share benchmark config + runbook, Maya will share sample payloads and traffic profile, and we'll aim to kick off the pilot week of Jan 4.
[09:02] Maya: great thanks all, look forward to the docs.
[09:06] Lena: thanks everyone.

[end of transcript — timestamps approximate; transcription automated so some words may be misheard, e.g., SAML as "Sam el", K M S spaced, KV cache transcribed as KV cash etc.]
